paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: replaces the stats row under the composer with provider and model, ba
lance or subscription quota, peak/off-peak pricing, and session spend.
# Bottom Info Bar
**English** | **中文**
### Join the DeepThinking beta group
Bugs, questions and feature requests get answered fastest in the group — scan the code, say what you
hit or what you want next, and it moves up the queue. The QR code expires periodically; open an iss
ue if it has stopped working.
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds an account information row under the composer: provider and mode
l, real balance or subscription quota, peak/off-peak pricing, and what this session has cost.
## What it shows
The bar follows the active session and picks one of three readings per provider (mutually exclusive,
nothing to switch by hand): **balance** shows the real balance from the provider's own API, **subsc
ription quota** shows each quota window's remaining allowance with its reset countdown (an exhausted
window stays visible at 0% instead of disappearing, flagged low), and **cloud billing** shows this
month's real spend from the official billing API. On top of that come four spend tallies — this sess
ion, today, last 30 days, all time — plus extras such as time and custom text. All four come from th
e plugin's own ledger, which **starts counting when the plugin first runs**: calls made before that
(or before you cleared the ledger) are not included, and hovering the spend writes out the exact sta
rt of the count. For the authoritative figure for a whole session, use the provider's own balance or
bill. In balance mode, hovering the balance expands it into topped-up and granted balances, so gift
ed credit is never conflated with the money you paid in.
On **DSH 0.2.1-rc.1 with the native activity/usage buttons**, the native line sits on top and the pl
ugin's account information on the line below. Clicking any plugin field still switches between **Ful
l** and **Compact** with the same height/fade animation: Full shows the native line, Compact collaps
es it. The native buttons keep their own click behavior and open Harness's details dialogs. Each of
the two native buttons can be hidden separately from the plugin's settings page. The context ring ke
eps its existing details and plugin settings.
On **older hosts**, clicking the bar still switches between **Full** and **Compact**: Full keeps the
legacy statistics row, Compact collapses it. Plugin fields remain identical in both modes. Compatib
ility is detected from the host's live extension entries, rather than a version string.
## Install
Recommended: open the DSH plugin page, choose **Add plugin**, and enter the npm package name — DSH f
etches the published package from npm, with no commands and no build:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Prefer the terminal? The same install from the command line:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
To run the newest code from the default branch instead of the latest release, paste the repository U
RL into the same field:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **restart DSH** — plugins are composed when the host starts, so a page refresh is not enough. I
n the desktop app, use **Plugins → Add plugin**; its profile is managed by the app and cannot be ins
talled into through the CLI. Other install methods (including Windows PowerShell) and troubleshootin
the CLI. Other install methods (including Windows PowerShell) and troubleshooting: docs/INSTALL.md.
The context usage ring keeps the native hover tooltip and opens a statistics panel when clicked. Bot
h overlays render outside the bottom bar so they do not change its contents.
## Settings
Plugin settings live under **Plugins → bottom-info-bar** and save as you change them. **Plugin infor
mation** and **notices** keep their field switches and colors. On modern hosts, **native information
** offers one switch per native button (session stats / usage) so either entry can be hidden; the ob
solete per-field statistics-row controls are omitted from the page, search results and enabled count
s. Their saved values are retained for older hosts. Older hosts still show the native field controls
. Resetting plugin fields or colors does not change Harness's native button preferences.
Plugin information is further grouped by billing mode — read only the block that matches your provid
er; each block's heading says which items carry data for it. Time zones, custom text, quota percenta
ge direction and billing data are separate sections:
API keys go in DSH under **Settings → Models**; subscriptions (Codex, OpenCode, Xiaomi Token Plan, C
ommand Code, MiniMax) read the local sign-in, and MiniMax requires a Subscription Key. Anything off
the list gets a not-supported hint instead of borrowed numbers.
## Spend and updates
The ledger requires a DSH runtime with Node.js 22.13 or newer. It keeps records and historical sessi
on indexes in a local disk database, reads bounded batches, and streams exports. Existing ledger fil
es are migrated once and retained for recovery; see Ledger storage and recovery.
Every model response records one entry (usage × unit price, locked the moment the response completes
) and survives restarts. The plugin checks npm once per DSH start: **automatic updates** (default) d
ownload in the background and take effect after you restart, **manual updates** only notify; a bad r
elease can be rolled back from settings. The ledger stores tokens and amounts, never conversation co
ntent; data stays under this end's `DSH_HOME` in `dsh-bottom-info-bar/` (default `~/.dsh/dsh-bottom-
info-bar/`, overridable via `DSH_BOTTOM_INFO_BAR_DATA_DIR`) and survives uninstall — export or clear
it from Billing data if you want a clean slate.
## Uninstall and roll back
Remove the plugin on the DSH plugin page (or `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-bottom-info-bar`)
and restart DSH: the native stats row comes back by itself and no plugin files are left behind. The
ledger is kept on purpose — export or clear it from **Billing data** before removing the plugin if y
ou want a clean slate. To go back a version instead, the update section offers **roll back to the pr
evious version** while a newer build is waiting for a restart, and after a failed update. Details: d
* while a newer build is waiting for a restart, and after a failed update. Details: docs/INSTALL.md.
